We got a list of templates. Need one that when applied to the given molecule reproduces the carbonyl-ene reaction (intramolecular). The description: carbonyl-ene reaction: alkene reacts with allylic hydrogen and carbonyl to form new C-C bond, forming a five-membered ring, hydroxyl. So the template likely is a carbonyl-ene transformation. Look at returned templates: there are several. Need to find which template matches our molecule. The molecule: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1... )... It's a bicyclic? Contains a carbonyl? Actually I see no carbonyl in SMILES: there is no =O. Wait the SMILES includes [C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])([F:18]) . So there is an OH attached to carbon 13, not carbonyl. The carbonyl may be part of a ketone elsewhere? I see no =O. So maybe the reaction is a carbonyl-ene where carbonyl is part of a ketone that will be formed? Actually forward reaction: carbonyl-ene forms carbonyl (C=O) and new C-C bond, but the description says C=O bond changes to C-O bond (so carbonyl becomes alcohol). So the retro step would break C-O bond to form carbonyl and C=C. So the retrosynthetic step: break C-O (hydroxyl) to form carbonyl and alkene. So we need a template that does that: a retro-ene (reverse of carbonyl-ene). The template likely has pattern: [C:...]-[C:...]([OH])>>[C]=[C] + carbonyl. Look at the templates list: first entry reaction_id 1229769 seems to involve Si and carbonyl etc not relevant. Second entry reaction_id 1209837: retro_smarts_template '[C:3]-[C:2](-[C:4])-[OH;D1;+0:1]>>C-C(=C)-C(=O)-[O;H0;D2;+0:1]-[C:2](-[C:3])-[C:4]'. That seems like breaking C-O to form carbonyl and C=C. That matches our need: product side is C-C(=C)-C(=O)-O... Actually the forward direction (retro) is breaking OH to form carbonyl and alkene. This seems plausible.

We need to check if this template applies to our molecule. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching with template_id? We need template_id integer. The search result gave reaction_id and template_hash but not template_id. The tool likely uses template_id as integer? The result includes reaction_id but not template_id. Maybe template_id is reaction_id? In other contexts, template_id is integer. Likely use reaction_id as template_id. Let's try with template_id 1209837. Use check tool.
